Q68814: City in southern Fujian, surrounding Xiamen together with Quanzhou.
Its Tulou — huge round earthen houses of the Hakka and Hokkien people — are partly a World Heritage Site.
Ancestral home of many Taiwanese and Southeast Asian Chinese families.
Known for narcissus flowers and pomelos.
Q336966: Capital of Qalyubiyya Governorate in the Nile Delta, north of Cairo.
An important railway junction between Cairo and the Delta cities.
Founded as a city in 1850; part of the Greater Cairo region.
Q304848: Oil city in western Heilongjiang; the name means 'great celebration'.
Founded after the Daqing Oil Field was discovered in 1959, China's largest oil field.
Mao's slogan 'In industry, learn from Daqing' made it a national model.
Known for wetlands and many lakes in the grassland around it.
Q57756: Port city in northeastern Jiangsu; the name means 'port connecting the clouds'.
Eastern end of the New Eurasian Land Bridge railway to Europe.
Huaguo Mountain nearby is said to be the home of the Monkey King from 'Journey to the West'.
Q2280: Capital of Belarus, on the Svislach River.
First mentioned in 1067; part of the Grand Duchy of Lithuania and Poland–Lithuania for centuries.
Almost completely destroyed in WWII and rebuilt in grand Stalinist style.
Seat of the Commonwealth of Independent States (CIS).
Q3551: Capital of Morocco, on the Atlantic at the mouth of the Bou Regreg river, opposite Salé.
Founded by the Almohads in the 12th century; the unfinished Hassan Tower dates from then.
A base of the Barbary corsairs (the 'Republic of Salé') in the 17th century.
Became the capital under the French protectorate in 1912; the Kasbah of the Udayas and the Mausoleum of Mohammed V are landmarks.
Q363479: City in northeastern Jiangxi, where Jiangxi borders Zhejiang, Fujian and Anhui.
Mount Sanqingshan, a Taoist mountain with granite peaks, is a World Heritage Site in the prefecture.
Wuyuan county is famous for its Huizhou-style villages and rapeseed flower fields.
Q34664: Capital of Hiroshima Prefecture, on the Ōta River delta.
Destroyed by the first atomic bomb used in war on 6 August 1945.
The Atomic Bomb Dome and Peace Memorial Park are reminders; the city campaigns for nuclear disarmament.
Known for okonomiyaki and the nearby Itsukushima Shrine with its 'floating' torii gate.
Q3306: Capital of Panama, at the Pacific entrance of the Panama Canal.
Founded in 1519, the first Spanish city on the Pacific coast of the Americas; Inca gold passed through it.
Destroyed by the pirate Henry Morgan in 1671 and rebuilt nearby; the old Casco Viejo is a World Heritage Site.
A banking hub with Latin America's most impressive skyline.
Q320704: Capital of Edo State in southern Nigeria.
Capital of the Kingdom of Benin, famous for its bronzes and once surrounded by huge earthen walls.
The British sacked the city in 1897 and took the Benin Bronzes, many of which are now being returned.
Seat of the Oba of Benin.
Q1473: The largest city in the Philippines by area and the biggest city on Mindanao.
Near Mount Apo, the highest mountain in the Philippines.
Home region of the Philippine eagle and known for durian.
Hometown of President Rodrigo Duterte, its long-time mayor.
Q48195: Iraq's main port, on the Shatt al-Arab near the Persian Gulf.
Founded in 636 as an Arab military camp; a centre of learning in the Islamic Golden Age.
Called the 'Venice of the East' for its old canals; said to be the port of Sinbad the Sailor.
One of the hottest cities in the world; near Iraq's big oil fields.
Q1741: Capital of Austria on the Danube, at the edge of the Vienna Woods.
Seat of the Habsburg emperors for centuries: Hofburg and Schönbrunn palaces.
The 'city of music' where Mozart, Beethoven, Haydn, Schubert and Strauss worked; also the city of Freud.
Hosts UN offices, OPEC and the IAEA; known for coffee houses and often ranked the most liveable city in the world.
Q54880: Venezuela's third-largest city, capital of Carabobo state.
The 1821 Battle of Carabobo nearby secured Venezuela's independence.
The country's main industrial centre, with car factories.
Q1491: Seat of government of Bolivia, in a canyon at about 3,600 m; the official capital is Sucre.
The highest seat of government in the world, overlooked by the snowy Illimani mountain.
Its Mi Teleférico cable-car network is the longest urban cable car system in the world.
Forms a metro area with El Alto on the plateau above.
Q244159: City in Jharkhand, called the 'Coal Capital of India' for the Jharia coalfield.
The Jharia coal fires have been burning underground for over 100 years.
Home of IIT (ISM) Dhanbad, an old mining school.
Q6809876: Town in East Champaran district, northern Bihar.
Has a traditional industry making buttons from mother-of-pearl shells.
Q72877: City in northern Shanxi, near the Great Wall and Inner Mongolia.
Capital of the Northern Wei dynasty (as Pingcheng) in the 5th century.
The Yungang Grottoes, with 51,000 Buddhist statues, are a World Heritage Site; the Hanging Temple clings to a cliff nearby.
Q373564: City in western Shandong on the Grand Canal.
Called the 'Venice of North China' for its lakes and canals; the Guangyue Tower is a landmark.
Was a prosperous trade stop on the Grand Canal during the Ming and Qing dynasties.
Q133118: City in southeastern Turkey, officially Şanlıurfa; called the 'City of Prophets'.
Göbekli Tepe, the world's oldest known temple (about 11,500 years old), is 12 km away.
Tradition says Abraham was born here; the sacred fish pools of Balıklıgöl honour him.
Known for isot pepper and urfa kebab.
Q109949: City next to Maputo, capital of Maputo Province; Mozambique's most populous city.
Has a port and Mozambique's biggest industrial area, including the Mozal aluminium smelter.
Q804027: Metropolitan region on the coast of São Paulo state, centred on Santos.
The Port of Santos is the busiest container port in Latin America.
Santos is home of Pelé's club, Santos FC; Cubatão is a big industrial hub.
A popular beach area for São Paulo residents.
Q205327: Capital of Kasai-Central province in DR Congo; formerly Luluabourg.
Lies near the Lulua River and on the railway from Ilebo to Lubumbashi.
Was the capital of the former Kasai-Occidental province.
Q360702: City in western Anhui at the northern foot of the Dabie Mountains.
Famous for Lu'an Guapian, a melon-seed-shaped green tea and one of China's top teas.
An old revolutionary base area of the Red Army.
Q360584: City in northwestern Anhui on the Ying River.
A big agricultural and labour-exporting region.
The Song writer Ouyang Xiu governed here and loved its West Lake of Yingzhou.
Q200054: The largest city of Jharkhand, also called Tatanagar.
Founded as India's first planned industrial city around the Tata steel plant (opened in 1912).
Named after Jamsetji Tata, founder of the Tata Group.
Known for its green planned layout and Jubilee Park.
Q23083: Metropolitan county in northern England, centred on Leeds and Bradford.
Grew with the wool and textile industry during the Industrial Revolution.
Includes Wakefield, Huddersfield and Halifax; the Brontë sisters lived at Haworth.
Bradford has a large South Asian community and is known for curry.
Q69060: Capital of Qinghai, the largest city on the Tibetan Plateau, at about 2,200 m.
An old Silk Road trading post; gateway to Tibet by the Qinghai–Tibet railway.
Near Kumbum (Ta'er) Monastery, birthplace of Tsongkhapa, founder of the Gelug school of Tibetan Buddhism.
Its Dongguan Mosque is one of the largest in northwest China.
Q189128: The largest city of Guanajuato in central Mexico.
Called the 'Shoe Capital of the World' for its leather and footwear industry.
Part of the Bajío region's car-manufacturing belt.
Known for its Arco de la Calzada and the yearly International Balloon Festival.
Q426996: Second most populous city of Sichuan, on the Jialing River.
Birthplace of Zhu De, founder of the Red Army, in Yilong county.
Q3780: Capital of Sierra Leone, on one of the world's largest natural harbours.
Founded in 1792 as a home for freed slaves from Britain and the Americas, hence its name.
Home of the Krio (Creole) people and Fourah Bay College (1827), the oldest university in West Africa.
Its old Cotton Tree was a symbol of freedom until it fell in 2023.
Q3659: Capital of Chad, on the Chari River opposite Cameroon.
Founded by the French as Fort-Lamy; renamed N'Djamena in the 1970s.
Close to Lake Chad, which has shrunk dramatically.
One of the hottest capital cities in the world.
Q59144: Port city on the Leizhou Peninsula in Guangdong, the southernmost port on the Chinese mainland.
Was the French concession of Kouang-Tchéou-Wan from 1898 to 1945.
Faces Hainan across the Qiongzhou Strait.
Home of China's South Sea Fleet and known for seafood.
Q15121208: Municipality in the State of Mexico, the most populous suburb of Mexico City.
The name means 'windy hill' in Nahuatl, after the wind god Ehecatl.
José María Morelos, hero of independence, was executed here in 1815.
Q6346: Capital of Indiana; nicknamed the 'Crossroads of America'.
Founded in 1821 as a planned capital in the centre of the state.
Hosts the Indianapolis 500, the largest single-day sporting event in the world, at its Motor Speedway.
Has more war memorials than any US city except Washington.
Q817269: City in North Kivu, eastern DR Congo, near the Virunga National Park and the Rwenzori Mountains.
A trading centre on the edge of the Ituri rainforest.
Has suffered from armed group violence and Ebola outbreaks.
Q372773: Capital of Chhattisgarh, which was created in 2000.
A big centre of steel, power and the rice trade.
Next to Naya Raipur, a new planned capital city.
Q2360428: The municipality of Tijuana in Baja California, the most populous municipality in Mexico.
Borders San Diego County in the USA.
Includes part of the Coronado Islands off the coast.
Q58576: City in southern Hebei, one of the oldest cities in northern China.
Capital of the Xing state in the Shang and Zhou dynasties.
Known for Xing kiln white porcelain and its role in China's glass and bicycle making.
Q194165: Jordan's third city, in the north near the Syrian border.
Built on Bronze Age settlements; possibly the ancient Arbila of the Decapolis.
A university city with Yarmouk University; called the 'Bride of the North'.
Near the Roman ruins of Umm Qais (Gadara).
Q289693: The third-largest city of the UAE, next to Dubai.
Ruled by the Al Qasimi dynasty since the 18th century.
Called the UAE's cultural capital; UNESCO's Arab Capital of Culture in 1998.
Alcohol is banned in the emirate.
Q19660: Capital of Romania, on the Dâmbovița River.
Once nicknamed 'Little Paris' for its Belle Époque buildings; has its own Arc de Triomphe.
Ceaușescu's Palace of the Parliament is one of the largest buildings in the world.
Legend links it to Vlad the Impaler, who ruled from here.
Q643883: City in Punjab, Pakistan, near the border with Jammu.
Makes most of the world's hand-stitched footballs, as well as surgical instruments and sports goods.
Birthplace of the poet Muhammad Iqbal.
Ancient Sagala, capital of the Indo-Greek king Menander.
Q83317: Iraq's second city, on the Tigris in the north.
Opposite the ruins of Nineveh, capital of the Assyrian Empire and once the largest city in the world.
Gave its name to muslin cloth.
Held by ISIS from 2014 to 2017; its Great Mosque of al-Nuri was destroyed and is being rebuilt.
Q211243: Capital of the Ningxia Hui Autonomous Region on the Yellow River; the name means 'silver river'.
Was the capital of the Tangut Western Xia dynasty; its royal tombs lie at the foot of the Helan Mountains.
A centre of the Hui Muslim minority and of a growing wine region.
Q11445: City in the cool highlands of East Java.
Historically Tumapel, centre of the Singhasari kingdom in the 13th century.
A university and tourist town; gateway to Mount Bromo.
Known for its Dutch colonial villas and apples from nearby Batu.
Q208318: Capital of Kaduna State, the former capital of Northern Nigeria.
Founded by the British under Lord Lugard around 1913; the name means 'crocodiles' in Hausa.
A railway hub and industrial centre with textile mills and an oil refinery.
Home of the Nigerian Defence Academy.
Q207749: City next to Mumbai on Salsette Island; part of the Mumbai metropolitan region.
India's first passenger train ran from Bombay to Thane in 1853.
Called the 'City of Lakes' for its many lakes.
Home to flamingo sanctuaries along Thane Creek.
Q217681: City in Shandong at the foot of Mount Tai.
Mount Tai is the most revered of China's Five Great Mountains; emperors performed sacrifices on its summit.
Climbing its 6,000+ steps to watch the sunrise is a famous tradition.
The Dai Temple in the city is one of China's largest temple complexes.
Q270: Capital of Poland, on the Vistula.
Became the capital in 1596 when King Sigismund III moved from Kraków.
About 85% destroyed in WWII after the 1944 Warsaw Uprising; its Old Town was rebuilt and is a World Heritage Site.
Birthplace of Chopin and Marie Curie; the Palace of Culture and Science was a gift from Stalin.
Q3748: Capital of Liberia, on the Atlantic at Cape Mesurado.
Founded in 1822 by the American Colonization Society for freed Black Americans.
Named after US President James Monroe.
Heavily damaged during Liberia's civil wars (1989–2003).
Q38545: Turkey's fifth-largest city, on the Seyhan River near the Mediterranean.
Centre of the fertile Çukurova plain, famous for cotton.
Its Roman Stone Bridge (Taşköprü) is one of the oldest bridges in the world still in use.
Famous for the spicy Adana kebab.
Q140631: The oldest city in Taiwan, in the southwest; capital of Taiwan for over 200 years until 1887.
The Dutch built Fort Zeelandia here in 1624; Koxinga drove them out in 1662.
Has more temples than any other Taiwanese city; called the 'Phoenix City'.
Known for its traditional snacks and the Anping Old Fort.
Q2219212: Metropolitan region in northern Mexico spanning Coahuila and Durango, centred on Torreón, Gómez Palacio and Lerdo.
Developed for irrigated cotton farming on land flooded by the Nazas and Aguanaval rivers.
Scene of heavy fighting in the Mexican Revolution and of Cárdenas's land reform.
The rivers end in inland lakes instead of flowing to the sea.
Q26323: City in eastern Guangdong, part of the Chaoshan region.
Hometown of many overseas Chinese in Southeast Asia.
Known for jade processing at the Yangmei jade market and for Teochew culture.
Q514796: City in western Shaanxi, on the Wei River.
Birthplace of the Zhou dynasty's ancestors and an early Qin capital.
The Famen Temple nearby holds a finger-bone relic of the Buddha.
Many famous Zhou bronze vessels were found here; it has a bronze museum.
Q10103: The largest city of the Riau Islands, on Batam island just 20 km south of Singapore.
Developed since the 1970s as a free-trade industrial zone for electronics and shipbuilding.
Linked with Rempang and Galang islands by the Barelang bridges.
Galang hosted a camp for Vietnamese boat people (1979–1996).
Q93338: City in south-central Turkey, called Aintab or Antep historically, about 100 km north of Aleppo.
Famous as the baklava and pistachio capital of Turkey and a UNESCO City of Gastronomy.
The Zeugma Mosaic Museum holds one of the largest collections of Roman mosaics, including the 'Gypsy Girl'.
Badly hit by the 2023 Turkey–Syria earthquakes.
Q16553: The largest city in the Bay Area and the 'Capital of Silicon Valley'.
Founded in 1777 as the first civilian Spanish town in California; it was California's first state capital.
Home of tech companies like Cisco, Adobe and Zoom.
Known for the mysterious Winchester Mystery House.
Q174461: Capital of Jharkhand, on the Chota Nagpur Plateau.
Centre of the movement that created Jharkhand state in 2000 for the tribal regions.
Called the 'City of Waterfalls' for falls like Hundru and Dassam nearby.
Hometown of cricket captain MS Dhoni.
